watches.name: OVNI Jumping Disc The Martian
watches.description: The OVNI Martian For centuries, Mars has captivated the human imagination. A world of iron-rich deserts, towering volcanoes and endless dust storms, its unmistakable ochre glow has inspired myths, scientific discovery and dreams of distant civilisations. It is the planet that has always seemed just close enough to tempt us, yet far enough to remain a mystery. The OVNI Martian captures that spirit. Its warm dégradé dial transitions from a deep burnt orange at its centre to a soft golden yellow around the edge, echoing the colours of the Martian horizon as sunlight filters through a sky filled with fine red dust. Inspired by the timeless vision of flying saucers that has fuelled human imagination for generations, the OVNI is engineered with the same obsession for exploration. Its 904L stainless steel case and signature doughnut-shaped sapphire crystal demand exceptional manufacturing precision, creating a seamless sculptural form while maintaining robust water resistance. At its heart beats the Swiss La Joux-Perret G101 Soigné, paired with Isotope’s exclusive Jumping Disc module. The lightweight aluminium time disc, finished with bespoke numerals and filled with Super-LumiNova®, glides beneath the crystal like a celestial body in silent orbit. Offering a 68-hour power reserve, the OVNI Martian combines space-age imagination with uncompromising Swiss watchmaking. Our journey is only beginning, and should we happen to meet the Martians, you’ll be the first to know. watches.name: Hydrium Grey Reef Shark
watches.description: Hydrium Grey Reef Shark Limited to 200 pieces. The Grey Reef Shark has an almost architectural quality to it: cold grey , precise and powerful without excess . Found around tropical coral reefs , particularly along drop-offs and areas of strong current, it is an important predator within these complex ecosystems . Research has also shown that grey reef sharks can transport nutrients from offshore waters back towards nutrient-poor reefs as they move between feeding and resting areas. This environment , and the animal’s understated presence within it, became the inspiration for the Hydrium Grey Reef Shark . The cold grey dial has a deliberately brutalist character, stripped back to the elements that define a Hydrium : the traditional Isotope Lacrima on the dial , our distinctive hands and the essential information required to read the time . Rather than illustrating the shark or relying on the usual visual clichés associated with it, we wanted its character to come through in the colour , texture and purpose of the watch itself . Super-LumiNova on the hands and diving bezel provides visibility in low light, while 300 metres of water resistance reflects the diving origins of the Hydrium collection . The Grey Reef Shark also introduces, for the first time , the Hydrium Bracelet , made from solid bead-blasted stainless-steel links and fitted with quick-release spring bars and a diver’s clasp with extension . The watch is also supplied with a grey FKM strap , allowing two very different interpretations of the same design . Inside is the Swiss Landeron 24 automatic movement , chosen for a watch designed to be worn and used rather than treated as an object of decoration. Our fascination with sharks has always been about the animals themselves and the extraordinary environments they inhabit. The Grey Reef Shark is deeply connected to the reef ecosystem , yet the species is today classified as Endangered on the IUCN Red List . The Hydrium Grey Reef Shark is our tribute to that remarkable animal , expressed not through imagery , but through the restrained colours , materials and functional character of the watch . watches.name: Isotope Mercury Alchemy
watches.description: Mercury Alchemy Limited to 40 pieces. What if Mercury could be transformed into gold? That question became the starting point for Mercury Alchemy . Inspired by the ancient pursuit of transmutation , we imagined our Mercury collection reinterpreted in a rich dark gold finish , paired with a deep green enamelled sunburst dial . The result is a watch whose colours feel inseparable. Dark gold and deep green have always belonged together. The cream numerals , created in our exclusive custom typeface , were drawn to echo the flowing architecture of the case , while the hand-finished, micro-painted cream hands bring warmth and exceptional legibility to the dial . Every detail has been carefully considered to create what we believe is one of the most harmonious interpretations of Mercury yet . The bracelet receives the same dark gold treatment as the case, while brushed centre links add a more refined character and a subtle contrast in finish. Like every Mercury bracelet , it incorporates a discreet on-the-fly micro-adjustment , allowing the fit to adapt effortlessly as your wrist changes throughout the day or across the seasons. For those who prefer leather, the cream nubuck strap is paired with a brushed dark gold buckle , finished with the same attention to elegance and durability. Beneath its distinctive appearance beats our calibre I-7 , based on the legendary ETA Peseux 7001 . Renowned for its slim profile and reliability, it offers a 42-hour power reserve and remains one of the finest hand-wound movements ever produced. Limited to just 40 pieces , Mercury Alchemy is not simply a new finish. It is the moment Mercury turns to gold. Now available with complimentary worldwide shipping. Ten pieces are available for immediate dispatch, with additional pieces arriving in September. watches.name: Mercury Seconds Society x Isotope
watches.description: Mercury Seconds Society x Isotope The Mercury Seconds Society x Isotope is a collector-led limited edition created with Seconds Society , the studio founded by Ash, Wahhaj and Ray . Seconds Society began in an unusual way. What started from an unfortunate scam experience became a close and trusted watch community , built around shared knowledge , collector instinct and a genuine appreciation for independent watchmaking . Today, Ash, Wahhaj and Ray work with independent makers to create limited editions that feel considered, distinctive and made by collectors, for collectors . For this collaboration , the Mercury becomes the canvas for a contemporary interpretation of the classic sector dial . The design takes inspiration from early precision watches , where balance , legibility and proportion were treated with almost architectural discipline . Here, those codes are not simply reproduced, but refined through a more modern Isotope language . The dial is hand-crafted in cold enamel with a layered cream-to-grey degradé , creating a soft transition of tone across the surface. Its sector layout introduces structure and calm , while the framed small seconds at 6 o’clock gives the composition a precise, instrument-like quality . The result is elegant rather than nostalgic, restrained rather than decorative, and quietly distinctive on the wrist . The design also reflects the energy of modern independent watchmaking , particularly the creativity seen today in Japan and China, where classical layouts are being revisited with confidence , intelligence and fresh perspective . That influence can be felt in the way the Mercury Seconds Society x Isotope respects vintage codes while avoiding pastiche . The Mercury case provides the ideal foundation for this idea. Sculpted from mirror-finished stainless steel , its polished surfaces and f luid geometry create a contemporary counterpoint to the disciplined dial architecture . This contrast is central to the watch: traditional in principle, modern in execution, and unmistakably Isotope in character . Inside is the Calibre I-7 , a Swiss Made , modified and regulated ETA Peseux 7001 . This hand-wound movement features a bespoke hand-finish visible through the sapphire exhibition case back . Limited to only 10 pieces , the Mercury Seconds Society x Isotope is a refined collector’s edition for those who value proportion, restraint, mechanical honesty and the quiet pleasure of a dial that rewards repeated looking . Available now. watches.name: Chronograph Moonshot Horizon
watches.description: Available Now: The Isotope Chronograph Compax Moonshot Horizon Isotope unveils the new Chronograph Compax Moonshot Horizon , a limited evolution of our award-winning chronograph platform, now presented in a sharper and more luminous configuration. Machined from Grade 5 Titanium , the Moonshot Horizon combines lightness, strength and a precise technical feel on the wrist. Its blue sunburst dial shifts from bright cyan to deeper tones as the light moves across it, while the orange rings around the registers take inspiration from the warm hues seen at the horizon , where colour, distance and atmosphere meet. The bezel combines a telemeter scale , used to estimate the distance of approaching storms , with a pulsometer scale for measuring heart rate , and keeping track of your passions. The visual language is influenced by the work of Moebius : graphic, architectural and imagined rather than nostalgic. It gives the Horizon a distinct identity within the Moonshot family, while keeping the watch firmly rooted in Isotope’s design codes . The dial construction remains one of the defining elements of the Moonshot . Instead of conventional open sub-dials, the chronograph registers use silver aluminium discs that partially cover the indications , revealing only the information needed to read them. It is a highly distinctive solution , developed to improve clarity while giving the chronograph its unmistakable character. The 41mm Grade 5 Titanium case is paired with the new titanium bracelet , now fitted with a quick-release button system for easier strap changes. Each watch is also supplied with the orange FKM CTS Moonshot strap , cut-to-size and fitted with a deployant clasp. The Moonshot platform has already been recognised by collectors and industry specialists. Last year, the Moonshot Terra Maris won the Public Choice Award in Toronto and the Innovation Award in Warsaw , confirming the strength of its concept, engineering and design. The new Moonshot Horizon continues that story in a more vibrant direction . Limited to 30 pieces , it is now available to ship. Inside beats the Swiss automatic Valjoux 7753 , one of the great automatic chronograph movements, chosen for its reliability, architecture and reputation . If the Grade 5 Titanium case , bespoke aluminium disc system and award-winning design were not serious enough, the Valjoux seals the deal . The name Moonshot was never chosen lightly. A moonshot is an attempt to do something difficult, ambitious and uncertain , not because it is easy, but because the idea is worth chasing . For Isotope , this meant r ethinking the chronograph display itself: keeping the familiar logic of a tricompax layout, but changing how the information is revealed. The result is not simply another chronograph with a new dial colour. It is a watch built around a solution no one else has achieved in quite this way : a mechanical chronograph where the sub-dials become rotating, partially hidden instruments, showing only what matters. For collectors looking for a chronograph that moves beyond the familiar , while remaining technically serious and deeply considered , the Moonshot Horizon sits exactly where its name suggests: at the edge of what already exists, looking further. Limited edition, available now for immediate shipping in very limited numbers. Technical Specifications: Case: Sandblasted Grade 5 Titanium, finished with a protective anti-fingerprint coating. watches.name: Mercury Altmann × Isotope
watches.description: Osaka Cloisonné Enamel For many years I wanted to create a watch inspired by the remarkable artistry of Japanese manhole covers . These objects belong to everyday urban life , yet they often display an extraordinary level of graphic sophistication , cultural symbolism , and civic pride . For a long time, however, I could not find the right way to approach the idea. In December 2024 I came across Björn Altmann’s book Manhole Covers of the World , and it became clear that I was not alone in recognising the artistic value of these designs. The book documents their typography , composition , and visual language with the same respect normally reserved for more conventional forms of art . After a short conversation with Björn , we realised there was a natural way to bring two artistic expressions together : his book and a very small series of watches. This collaboration resulted in something entirely new at this level of craftsmanship . The dials are made using grand feu cloisonné enamel on sterling silver bases . Fine silver wires form the structure of the design while multiple layers of vitreous enamel are applied and fired individually. Each colour requires its own application and firing stage before the dial can be hand-finished. Because of the complexity of the pattern and the number of firing cycles required , completing the five dials took almost a full year. The manhole cover depicted originates from Osaka and features Osaka Castle at its centre, framed by flowing water and cherry blossoms in bloom . The surrounding motifs symbolise the city’s history, seasonal renewal, and its r elationship with water. The Japanese characters cast into the original cover read 大阪市 (Ōsaka-shi) , meaning Osaka City . This identifies it as an official municipal design rather than a decorative reinterpretation. This connection to real urban infrastructure is precisely what makes these objects so compelling . They are functional, civic, and quietly artistic . Translating this manhole cover into a watch dial was not about simplification but about fidelity . Every line, colour, and proportion was carefully adapted to preserve the spirit of the original design while reinterpreting it through traditional watchmaking techniques . Only five dials were produced. Each watch includes a copy of Manhole Covers of the World , signed by Björn Altmann. — José Miranda Co-founder, Isotope Watches About Björn Altmann Björn Altmann is an independent designer , illustrator, and typographer with more than 17 years of experience in the creative industry. With a strong focus on branding and a longstanding interest in watches , he has contributed to the watch industry as an illustrator, dial designer, and type specialist. Based in London for many years, he worked both within agencies and independently, collaborating with major international brands . He has built a strong reputation within the watch world through collaborations with established brands , independent makers , and private collectors , contributing across illustration , dial design , typography , and special commissions . His work extends to major editorial and publishing projects , including the illustration of more than 500 watch references for a landmark publication, and has appeared in industry publications, auction projects, and collector-focused platforms . Björn is the author of Manhole Covers of the World , published by the Swiss publisher niggli. Cloisonné Enamel Dial Production Because of the complexity of the pattern , and in order to keep the project commercially viable , we spent nearly twelve months developing a p roduction method that would allow us to create just five dials. watches.description: Available Now: Chronograph Moonshot Thunderclap A storm captured in titanium . The first Isotope chronograph with a telemeter scale , limited to just 30 pieces . The Isotope Moonshot Chronograph Thunderclap captures the drama of a storm in mechanical form. Limited to just 30 pieces worldwide , this special edition introduces a striking new visual direction to the Moonshot platform and marks a milestone for the brand: the first Isotope chronograph to feature a telemeter scale . Developed in collaboration with Matt Smith-Johnson, known as Teenage Grandpa , Thunderclap combines proven Moonshot architecture with a bold new aesthetic language . A Collaboration with Teenage Grandpa The Moonshot Chronograph Thunderclap was created together with artist and designer Matt Smith-Johnson (Teenage Grandpa) , whose fearless visual style and instinct for the unexpected made him a natural partner for reinterpreting the Moonshot. “The first time I met Matt, I was immediately struck by his energy, sharp mind, and design originality. He had a genuine connection with the Moonshot, which led me to invite him to create his own interpretation of it. The result is bold and unexpected, a version that could only come from the mind of Teenage Grandpa.” — José Miranda, Co-Founder, Isotope Watches The result is a Moonshot that feels sharper and more expressive , while remaining faithful to the architecture collectors already appreciate . A Storm in Grey and Purple Thunderclap retains the full technical platform of the Moonshot while introducing a new visual language. The case is crafted from sandblasted Grade 5 titanium , presented without DLC coating so the metal’s natural character remains visible. The dial creates a striking interplay of texture and colour: • Grey embossed dimple dial , evoking charged storm clouds • Metallic purple Moondisc sub-dials that shimmer as light moves across them • Purple chronograph pushers delivering a vivid flash of colour on the case flank The Thunderclap is Industrial at first glance . Electric on closer inspection. Introducing the Telemeter Scale The Moonshot Chronograph Thunderclap introduces the first telemeter scale ever used on an Isotope watch. Historically , telemeters were used to measure the distance between a visible event and the sound it produces . By starting the chronograph when lightning appears and stopping it when thunder is heard, the scale indicates how far away the storm is. A scale born from science , speed , and instinct . Perfectly suited to a watch called Thunderclap . Proven Moonshot Architecture Thunderclap maintains everything that defines the Moonshot platform: • Identical Moonshot case architecture • The same chronograph movement configuration • 100m water resistance • Meticulous finishing throughout Everything that defines the Moonshot remains intact. Only the interpretation is new. Limited edition, available now for immediate shipping in very limited numbers. watches.description: Old Radium Polar Enamel The Old Radium Polar Enamel explores the collection through c ontrast and clarity . Inspired by early pilot and field watches, as well as the instruments used for navigation in extreme environments, this edition focuses on legibility , balance , and permanence . The dial is crafted in white enamel , chosen for its depth , stability , and long-term durability . Unlike painted surfaces, enamel does not fade with time and offers a subtle, mineral-like finish that interacts naturally with light. Against this bright base, the Old Radium numerals and markings stand out with exceptional clarity , reinforcing the functional character of the design . The warm tone of the Super-LumiNova recalls the appearance of vintage radium dials while remaining entirely safe . Sword hands and Arabic numerals follow traditional pilot-watch proportions , ensuring instant readability in all conditions. A discreet date window provides everyday practicality without disturbing the overall balance of the dial . The 40mm case measures just 10.1mm in thickness , giving the watch a notably slim profile for an automatic model . This restrained proportion enhances comfort and wearability while preserving the solid presence expected of a classic tool watch . An anti-reflective sapphire crystal protects the dial, and the open titanium case back reveals the Swiss automatic movement inside. Each watch is individually numbered and produced as a limited edition of 300 pieces . Technical Specifications Brushed CuSn8 Bronze case, sandblasted Titanium exhibition case back. watches.name: Hydrium Ice Fall
watches.description: Introducing the Hydrium Ice Fall , our first watch to feature a stone dial . At its heart sits a Brazilian amethyst , cut to an extraordinary thickness of just 0.4 mm . A stone born in warmth , transformed to look like ice . There is something beautifully contradictory about that. The inspiration came from a visit to the Ice Cave of the Mer de Glace in Chamonix , where light filters through ancient frozen walls , revealing veins , fractures , and flowing textures beneath the surface. As the glacier slowly breathes and melts, droplets and rivulets create a quiet choreography of light and motion. We wanted to capture that frozen moment in time . Finding the right stone was essential. We searched for a natural, organic material capable of reproducing the translucency, depth, and crystalline structure of ice . Amethyst proved to be the perfect choice. When cut ultra-thin, it reveals internal veins and luminosity that feel unmistakably glacial . This translucency serves another purpose. The dial allows glimpses of the La Joux-Perret movement beneath, with its generous 68-hour power reserve , adding mechanical depth to the visual experience without disturbing the calm surface above . The hands echo this language. Sharp , purposeful forms inspired by the metal spikes of mountaineering boots and the geometry of icicles , designed to cut cleanly through the dial without overpowering it. The heat-blued seconds hand and Super-LumiNova-filled indexes introduce subtle blue tones, reinforcing the cold , pure aesthetic of glacial water flowing into surrounding lakes and rivers. Limited to just 20 pieces , the Hydrium Ice Fall celebrates winter , ice , and the b eauty of transformation . It also marks the beginning of Isotope’s 10th anniversary year . Cold by design. Unmistakably Isotope. watches.name: Hydrium Snooty
watches.description: Lord Fauntleroy Snooty, Esq. Baby Boomer, Lord 🎩 Fauntleroy Snooty first dabbled in art during the pre-punk era , before life took one of its curious turns and found him spraying packing crates for the British Army at Greenham Common . From there, he made the rather more conventional leap into banking — a career that proved both substantial and suitably respectable , until the lure of creativity proved too strong to resist. Upon retiring, Snooty stumbled across this “ newfangled ” thing called the Internet and, with it, the world of Urban Street Art . After immersing himself in the modern scriptures Exit Through the Gift Shop and Bomb It , he re-emerged in 2013 with renewed purpose and a spray can in hand , setting his sights on the streets of Shoreditch and Hoxton. His 2015 work on the Shoreditch Art Wall caught the eye of the Financial Times, Street Art Weekly, and Street Art Germany . Even the venerable Gilbert & George were spotted strolling by . That same year, Snooty’s six submissions to the SSOSVA Christmas Show in Ealing sold out entirely — “red-dotted” in record time — amid rumours that Banksy himself might appear (he didn’t, but the forums were delighted nonetheless). From East to West London , Soho to Los Angeles , Snooty’s works have graced galleries , TV screens — including Million Dollar Listing — and, quite discreetly, a number of Beverly Hills mansions whose f amous owners prefer to remain unnamed . After a brief escapade at Glastonbury — posting stickers in Hospitality and fraternising with the Chemical Brothers — Snooty was overheard announcing: “Ladies and gentlemen, I’m off! You wait ’til I’m dead — you’ll see I was right!” Naturally, no one quite believes him . His agent & mentor insists it’s merely another of his cunning plans — word has it, he’s already plotting a surprise appearance at Art Basil. The Hydrium Snooty Against the advice of several sensible people, Lord Fauntleroy Snooty has agreed to place his name on a dive watch . This marks his first collaboration with Isotope , a brand that understands the importance of doing things properly while appearing not to care at all . The result is a f ully capable Swiss-made Hydrium , discreetly misbehaving beneath the surface and entirely unapologetic about it . Produced in a strictly unnecessary limitation of 20 pieces , the Hydrium Snooty has already attracted rumours . Snooty insists this is a one-off . His agent refuses to comment . We have heard this before. A future classic , or an expensive misunderstanding . Possibly both. Take one . Say nothing . ----------------------------- One Escaped… Against all probability, Hydrium Snooty #05/20 has become available. Its original custodian, after much soul-searching, tea-drinking and what we can only assume was an unfortunate lapse in judgement, has relinquished his allocation. Lord Fauntleroy Snooty , naturally, has already issued a statement: “One simply cannot have people abandoning perfectly splendid watches. Fortunately, I’ve instructed my people to release it back into the wild. Do try to keep up.” So here we are. One watch. One opportunity. #05/20 is now available to whoever is quick enough to claim it. Once it has gone, the edition returns to being exactly what it was always meant to be: strictly limited to 20 pieces , with no hidden stock, no secret reserve, and no persuasive letters accepted from distant cousins of the aristocracy. Take one. Say nothing. watches.description: When Signs Come to Life Sometimes you walk past a shop window, spot something unusual and press your nose against the glass. Just as your curiosity peaks, you notice the familiar “ Will Return ” sign and realise that what you want is out of reach . In a slightly different setting, this was exactly the experience of many watch enthusiasts when we launched our signature diver’s watch, the HydriumX Will Return , in 2021. Inspired by the iconic sign and featuring a white dial filled with Swiss Super-LumiNova , red hands and a light blue bezel with a red Lacrima marker, it captured a universal moment in a completely novel way. The idea was playful and unexpected , and its success took us by surprise . All 100 pieces of this limited edition sold out quickly, and the HydriumX Will Return was later honoured with a nomination for the Grand Prix d’Horlogerie de Genève (GPHG) in 2022 . Its colourful character opened the door for more extravagant designs , not only at Isotope but also for other brands. It became a quiet trailblazer. Yet, as a limited edition, bringing it back was never an option. However, when you put up a “Will Return” sign, at some point you must return . Introducing the Wall Return Back by popular demand and thanks to the many messages asking us to revive the Will Return , we are proud to present its larger-than-life sequel . The Will Return has grown to King Size and now hangs on your wall. With the same recognisable design that made the original so beloved , the Wall Return is our playful tribute to the idea that started it all. It's 35 cm in diameter and domed crystal brings life to any room. The aluminium case is finely crafted and preserves the serrated edge of a traditional diving bezel, a detail that unmistakably belongs to the Isotope design language. For this clock we stepped away from our usual Swiss movements and chose a reliable Seiko sweeping quartz movement (battery not included). A wall clock receives far less physical interaction , so reliability , low maintenance and a smooth sweeping second hand made perfect sense. It still provides a mechanical vibe , only now with the bonus of remaining wonderfully quiet. The Wall Return keeps the full colour scheme of the original HydriumX Will Retur n and features a fully luminous dial , allowing it to remain an eye-catcher day and night . It is limited to 300 pieces. Introducing the Exit Clock Some moments invite a return . Others insist on a rapid exit . Whether sparked by urgency or a shift in the atmosphere, the signal to move can appear without warning. Inspired by one of our most original watches, the HydriumX Exit , we created a wall clock that brings this playful idea into a larger canvas. The Exit watch gained attention for its clever use of a l uminous dial that reveals a cheeky twist in the dark . The little man escaping the dial became one of our most recognisable and humorous touches, and its creativity inspired more than a few releases in the industry . The Exit Clock takes that concept and magnifies it. The design is bold yet minimal, instantly readable and unmistakably Isotope . Its fully l uminous background transforms when the lights go out, revealing the iconic running figure escaping the scene . It is a reminder that sometimes the most memorable moments are the ones where you make a swift and stylish exit. Craftsmanship remains at the heart of this clock. It shares the same 35 cm in diameter, domed crystal and aluminium case as the Wall Return, creating a consistent Isotope aesthetic . It is powered by the same smooth sweeping Seiko movement and built to last a lifetime. The Exit Clock is limited to 200 pieces. Two Icons. One Identity. Unmistakably Isotope. watches.name: Hydrium Trippy
watches.description: Hydrium Trippy - Moiré Edition Introducing the latest experiment in our Hydrium collection, the Hydrium Trippy . While the Hydrium line includes serious professional divers such as the Hydrium Pro Nordblad and colourful pop culture designs like the Will Return or Exit editions, the Trippy takes a more playful and complex turn, combining the reliability of a diver’s tool watch with an unexpected Moiré dial experience . Why Moiré? The dial of the Trippy is no mere backdrop. By layering patterns , we created a true Moiré effect , a subtle optical dance that changes every second, every minute and every hour. The texture is never static . Your watch dial comes alive, turning into a kinetic graphic that brings a smile even while you are timing a dive or a project with the Mushroom hands . Mushrooms, mischief, and inspiration Mushrooms have a long legacy as symbols of altered states , wonder and mischievous glamour . We borrowed this spirit not to glamorise anything irresponsible but to celebrate a mindset of curiosity and discovery . In the hit series The Studio (Season 1, Episode 9, “CinemaCon”), the characters played by Zoë Kravitz , Bryan Cranston and Seth Rogen accidentally consume a generous amount of mushrooms at a party, creating one of the funniest scenes in recent television. The story was inspired by Seth Rogen’s real-life experience of unknowingly eating a large amount of mushrooms before a podcast interview. We nodded to that same spirit of playful confusion for the Trippy . The dial is designed to surprise , evoke curiosity, and remind us that even ordinary moments can become extraordinary . But unlike the show , you do not need to ingest anything . The Trippy offers all the fun you need, even in the dark . The diver’s DNA remains intact This is still Hydrium at heart , built with the same robust case , 300m of water resistance , and a Swiss-made La Joux-Perret movement with a 68-hour power reserve . The fun is on the surface , but the substance beneath remains t rue to our diver’s heritage . Limited to 20 “doses” To keep the magic rare, the Hydrium Trippy is limited to only 20 pieces worldwide. Each one is individually numbered . Join us on this playful side of dive-watching . Wear it confidently, enjoy the living dial, and remember that the Trippy will give you all the fun you need . watches.description: Oracle Time x Isotope Mercury Vitreous Orange and Green Watch news platform Oracle Time and British watchmaker Isotope proudly announce the launch of the Oracle Time x Isotope Mercury Vitreous Green and Orange – two highly limited timepieces showcasing the striking beauty and complexity of vitreous enamel dials in radically different tones. Over the past two years, Isotope has demonstrated a commitment to bringing Métiers d’Art to a more accessible price point , with techniques as varied as marquetry and cloisonné enamel . This latest collaboration takes that vision a step further with vitreous enamel dials given a colourful twist, offering exceptional craftsmanship without compromise on aesthetics or integrity. The Dials Enamel has a storied history spanning millennia: first developed in ancient Egypt , refined in China with exquisite cloisonné techniques , and perfected in Europe . By the late 17th century , Geneva watchmakers were applying enamel to dials , combining centuries of decorative artistry with Swiss precision . The Mercury Vitreous series continues this legacy , showcasing Grand Feu enamel dials that highlight both traditional craftsmanship and contemporary design . While vitreous enamel is not new to British watchmaking , the Mercury Vitreous series introduces a textured silver leaf base beneath translucent enamel layers . Each dial is painstakingly built up , layer by layer, fired at extremely high temperatures to achieve unmatched depth and vibrancy . The process is demanding and highly risky – even the slightest imperfection renders a dial unusable – but the results are undeniably breathtaking . These Grand Feu Enamel dials are housed in the compact 38mm Mercury case, tailored to complement each dial tone in two distinct executions: Vitreous Orange – a molten, volcanic hue framed by a matte black DLC-coated steel case with a matching black FKM rubber strap. Vitreous Green – a bright spearmint tone paired with a fully bead-blasted stainless-steel case and soft grey FKM strap. Both versions feature a clean, minimalist dial free from numerals or distractions, allowing the enamel to speak for itself. Each watch is fitted with a domed sapphire crystal with anti-reflective coating, an exhibition caseback, and the custom-engraved I-7 calibre – Isotope’s regulated interpretation of the hand-wound ETA Peseux 7001 . Both versions are strictly limited to 25 numbered pieces , making them true collector’s items, and are available for shipping the following day. watches.description: Isotope OVNI Founders edition An unidentified object has landed on your wrist. The Isotope OVNI reimagines timekeeping by transforming t he entire dial into a living, moving work of art . Inspired by the pioneering spirit of ' Lost in Space' and designed to echo the silhouette of a flying saucer , the OVNI is more than a watch; it is the embodiment of Isotope’s tenth anniversary , a tribute to founder José Miranda’s creative journey, and a bold step toward the future. From the streamlined Rider Jumping Hour in 2016, to the groundbreaking GMT 0º , to the acclaimed Goutte d'Eau and Hydrium , Isotope has consistently challenged conventions. More recent innovations include the Moonshot , which introduced our signature moondiscs , and the Flyway , featuring the hyperbolic paraboloid sapphire crystal , both examples of how the team Isotope transforms technical ingenuity into visual poetry . The OVNI carries this lineage forward, evolving the moondisc concept into an entirely new language of time, powered by our proprietary jumping disc module. Named after the Iberian/French abbreviation for UFO , the OVNI unites heritage and imagination, precision and play. With its domed saucer-shaped case , luminous numerals , and sculptural presence , it feels as though it belongs among the stars, while effortlessly wearing here on Earth. The OVNI Founders Edition is a strictly limited release , created to mark Isotope’s first decade of independent watchmaking . Each piece is individually numbered , underscoring its exclusivity and significance . As the brand’s tenth-anniversary watch , it represents both the daring spirit of our beginnings and a collector’s milestone destined to become a cornerstone of the Isotope story. Space-Age Craftsmanship Crafting a flying-saucer-shaped watch is no small feat. The OVNI’s 904L stainless steel case and doughnut-shaped sapphire crysta l demand extraordinary tolerances to achieve both seamless curves and watertight performance. At its core beats the Swiss La Joux-Perret G101 Soigné movement, enhanced with Isotope’s exclusive jumping disc complication . The lightweight aluminium time disc , finished with bespoke numerals and filled with Super-LumiNova® , orbits beneath the crystal like a celestial body. With 68 hours of power reserve and accuracy tested in four positions, the OVNI is as reliable as it is otherworldly . Complementing the case is an elegantly crafted stainless steel bracelet , designed specifically for the Flyway . While seamlessly integrated with the case, the Flyway is not an integrated design, allowing you to easily swap straps and personalize the watch to match your mood and style . watches.description: Metiers d'Art: Innovation and Craftsmanship at the Heart of Isotope Considering making your dream dial a reality? Email info@isotopewatches.com to arrange a call with Isotope Watches Co-Founder José Miranda. Micro Marquetry is a truly unique art form, and we’re proud to offer bespoke watches crafted with this incredible technique. Whether it’s a single timepiece or a set for your family or group, each watch dial is handmade using natural straw, a living material that ensures every piece is one of a kind, even if the designs appear similar. There’s no better way to honour remarkable moments and lasting bonds than with a custom timepiece from Isotope Watches. We work closely with you at every stage, crafting a watch that’s as distinctive as your story. The result is a one-of-a-kind creation that’s both meaningful and enduring—an investment in time and memory. At Isotope, innovation isn’t just a guiding principle—it’s our heartbeat. Through daring designs, intricate complications, and pioneering materials, we continually push boundaries. Our precision mechanical movements captivate with their beauty and functionality, while bespoke modules add imaginative and captivating complications. Yet, for us, technical ingenuity is never enough without aesthetic charm. Our mission is to harmonize both, ensuring Isotope creations remain as accessible as possible. This balance drives us to collaborate with exceptional craftspeople to bring extraordinary visions to life. One of the most mesmerizing examples is our work with straw marquetry, a centuries-old decorative art that is as rare as it is exquisite. Originating in Asia and introduced to Europe through trade, straw marquetry flourished in 17th-century France, where it adorned the furniture and walls of the aristocracy. Over the years, this delicate craft has waned, with fewer than ten artisans practising micro marquetry today. Among these passionate artisans is Bernardo d’Orey, a remarkable artist crafting stunning dials for Isotope’s unique Mercury collection from his Paris workshop. From dyeing and preparing the straw to meticulously cutting and arranging each piece, every step is done entirely by hand. Since straw is a natural material, no two pieces are alike, making each dial a singular work of art. Its natural sheen reflects light in captivating ways, bringing patterns and hues to life as no other material can. Creating these dials is a painstaking process that requires years of skill and patience. Bernardo’s precision leaves no room for error as he transforms simple straw into intricate, breathtaking designs. The result is a dial unlike anything else in watchmaking—a true testament to the artistry and dedication behind it. For those seeking something truly personal, we invite discerning collectors to commission a bespoke Mercury watch with a custom straw marquetry dial. Prices commence at £4,000 + VAT per watch, highlighting the craftsmanship and distinctive nature of each creation. To initiate the creation of your watch, we ask for a deposit of £2,000 + VAT. Please email us at info@isotopewatches.com to arrange a video call or an in-person meeting with the Co-Founder of Isotope Watches to begin your bespoke project. More than a timepiece, it’s a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity to express your taste through one of horology’s rarest and most beautiful arts. This watch features a world-first and exclusive sub-dial design , refining the classic tricompax layout for improved readability and functionality. Housed under a double-domed sapphire crystal, it breaks away from conventional chronograph norms with a design that’s as daring as it is functional. CNC-machined from a single block of Grade 5 Titanium and hand-finished to a dark, stealthy sheen, the Moonshot pays tribute to the space-age chronographs of the 1970s, reimagined through a contemporary lens. Its design draws heavily from ‘The Incal’, the iconic 1980s graphic novel by Jodorowsky and Moebius—a deep influence on Isotope founder José Mendes Miranda, who sought to capture the novel’s complex themes and pioneering visuals. (Note: the authors and their estates are not affiliated with this watch.) Inside, you'll find a choice of Swiss automatic movements : either the ETA Valjoux 7753 or the Landeron 73. The 41mm case (49.5mm lug-to-lug) has a distinctive silhouette that sets a new direction for future Isotope designs. After four years of development, this is Isotope’s most ambitious watch yet. The rotating sub-dial discs required careful weight calibration for accuracy, a technical challenge that led to an exclusive and bespoke solution. Each Moonshot Stealth is individually numbered, supplied with both a Grade 5 Titanium bracelet and a cut-to-size black FKM strap with a butterfly deployant clasp. The Materialisation of a Fictional Universe "I’ve always been drawn to dystopian fiction and imagined worlds," says José Mendes Miranda. "With the Moonshot , we wanted to step away from the sea of vintage-inspired chronographs and create something that doesn’t exist yet, a watch that feels like it belongs to a different reality. This is our most complex piece to date , and a true labour of love." watches.name: Isotope x Revolution Mercury
watches.description: The Isotope x Revolution Mercury is now sold out in the U.K. However, our project partner still has a few pieces available in the U.S. and Singapore, with worldwide shipping. Don’t miss out—visit them here . The Isotope x Revolution Mercury is our latest collab and it's an outstanding example of original design and polishing techniques. This 150-piece limited edition is inspired by the multiple meanings of Mercury — a liquid metal, a train and the Roman god that is a bearer of positive tidings. Revolution's Wei Koh and Jose Miranda's Isotope founder created our latest limited edition — the Isotope × Revolution Mercury Limited Edition . It is a fully polished stainless steel watch with the first-ever mirror-polished convex dial . Arriving at the perfect polish for the case, dial and hands was an infinitely painstaking effort, but arriving at its design is a process that will pleasantly blow your mind. The watch is an abstract exploration of the polysemy of Mercury, as a liquid metal, the American Art Deco streamliner and the Roman god of positive tidings. Much like experiencing art, the great appeal and joy of beholding the Mercury watch lie not merely in its visual impact but in its abstractions, and this is made possible only when a watch was authentically designed from scratch with little constraints or preconceptions of how it should look. The Polysemy of Mercury A consistent feature across all Isotope watches is the subtle, and often playful, integration of the brand’s 'lacrima' logo (Latin for "teardrop") into various elements of the watch, including the lugs, markers, dial, or hands. The teardrop shape was inspired by the Kitchen Clock designed by Max Bill for Junghans in 1956, a piece that José grew up with. Additionally, up until this point, a subversive dress watch was missing in Isotope’s catalogue. Hence, that became the starting point for the Mercury . Subsequently, the Isotope team began toying with the idea of liquid metal droplets. Mercury , known by its chemical symbol Hg, is most famous for its fluidity at room temperature. This was reflected in the Isotope logo on the dial of the Mercury watch, serving as the noon marker, featuring a primary droplet accompanied by a smaller residual droplet. From there, the creative process unfolded like a mind map with the team drawing inspiration from the polysemy of Mercury . The case design found its muse in the Mercury train, a set of high-speed passenger trains operated by the New York Central Railroad in the mid-20th century. Offering faster speeds, improved comfort and a futuristic appearance, the Mercury was part of a larger effort to make train travel more attractive as railroads sought to compete with the growing popularity of automobiles and aeroplanes. Inaugurated in 1936, the Mercury train was the brainchild of industrial designer Henry Dreyfuss . It epitomized the Art Deco and Streamline Moderne design movements of its era, characterized by sleek, aerodynamic exteriors boasting smooth planes, horizontal lines and curved corners. Comprised of three parts, the case of the Mercury watch measures 38mm in diameter and 44.5mm lug to lug with a height of 10mm. It is characterized by rounded, sweeping lines and gentle curves. While polishing is often employed to emphasize flat planes and sharp angles, it is equally adept at accentuating curves and domes, creating a sense of fluidity and tactile quality that is enormously satisfying. The shape of the lugs was derived from the brand’s logo, each being half of the teardrop’s form. The lugs are raised slightly from the caseband, giving it a wonderfully tactile profile. The caseback is concave and articulates around the wrist nicely. It has a knurled and polished crown with the 'lacrima' logo. Despite being conceived as a dress watch, it offers a water resistance of 100 meters. The Pursuit of the Perfect Polish Another dimension of Mercury that inspired the watch was the Roman God Mercury, also known as Hermes in Greek myth

watches.description: (Eng.) Limited Edition Isotope Old Radium ‘Black Ink Bronze’ x Espiral do Tempo “Paint It Black”, sang The Rolling Stones in 1966. “Back in Black”, sang AC/DC in 1980. “Back To Black” , sang Amy Winehouse in 2007. Faced with the profusion of colourful dials that have characterized watchmaking in recent years, Portuguese magazine Espiral do Tempo chose to return to a primary and essential colour for its limited edition in partnership with British brand Isotope : black. In a run of 65 pieces, the Old Radium ‘Black Ink Bronze’ x Espiral do Tempo gives prominence to a completely black lacquered dial that is unprecedented in Isotope 's Old Radium collection and pairs it with a bronze case that provides the ideal contrast for a watch that can be classic... but also very rock n' roll. Black is the colour of rock n' roll. It's the colour of romance and magic; it symbolizes simplicity and elegance. But it's also the first colour used in a printer and the most used colour in the universe where Espiral do Tempo operates that of publication, printing, and reading. Black is the easiest colour to read in contrast to the white pages of the magazine; it's also the colour of text used against a white background for the best readability on our website espiraldotempo.com BLACK AND BRONZE Black is also the colour worn by the lead singers of the best known rock bands. The great mentor of the epic Portuguese Discoveries , Infante Dom Henrique , is traditionally depicted dressed in black — and the specific choice of the 40mm diameter by 10.1mm thick case material is precisely associated with Portuguese maritime history, as bronze has always been a widely used metal alloy in navigation due to its anti-corrosive properties. In addition to offering a beautiful contrast with the black dial, bronze also takes on a very special and personalized hue; because it's a living metal alloy, it acquires a patina that becomes unique in contact with each person's skin and considering the air quality or even the proximity to the sea. The bronze chosen for the Old Radium ‘Black Ink Bronze’ x Espiral do Tempo is CuSn8 — an alloy with 92% copper, 7.7% tin, and 0.3% phosphorus that acquires a controlled patina for a unique look. All metal components of the case are bronze, except for the titanium case back that supports the sapphire glass. Protected by an anti-reflective sapphire glass, the thin epoxy enamel dial has the style and readability of ancient aviator watches that inspired the Old Radium collection. It was also instrumental in building luxurious ocean liners and planes that ensured the country's safety during the 'Battle of Britain.' Additionally, steel contributed to the victory of its powerful race cars on tracks worldwide. Steel is also the main ingredient of some of the fundamental watchmaker's tools. Now it is steel that takes Isotope's HydriumX to the next level, featuring a bezel made entirely from this historically important metal alloy for the very first time. watches.description: Limited edition Isotope Hydrium California Diving was profoundly different a century ago. What is now the territory of many enthusiastic amateur divers was a field for hardened and determined professionals back then. It wasn't until the documentary 'The Silent World' debuted in 1956 that the general public became more aware of the wonders below sea level. With his ship 'Calypso,' for over two years, underwater pioneer Jacques-Yves Cousteau sailed the Red Sea, Mediterranean Sea, Persian Gulf, and the Indian Ocean, shooting over 25 kilometres of film underwater. Rapid equipment improvements in the following years made the beauty of underwater life more accessible for amateurs to explore, turning diving into a sport. But in the early days of diving, it was a hazardous endeavour, very much like exploring a different planet. Today, a diving watch is a backup for the diving computer, but in those days, it was a vital piece of equipment. Before the 1950s, dive watches were fairly uncommon for most people because there was no market for them. The majority of professional divers, apart from a few scientists and explorers, were in military units. Their watches were made by government order. As legibility was important, brands played with luminous material to make the dials read as easily. As even the slightest error can make the difference between life and death, there needs to be no confusion at all about the current time. On July 15, 1942, Rolex was awarded a patent (Brevet No.221643, now expired) for a dial with Roman numerals at the top half of the dial and Arabic ones at the bottom. They advertised them as 'error-proof' dials, as there is even a more distinct difference between them. Panerai would also start using these types of dials for their watches, supplied by Rolex and made by Stern Frères around 1944, although they claimed to have already had a prototype with this type of dial in 1936. As you can see, the 'California dial' history is like murky water with (too) many myths. This is also regarding the name, which this type of dial didn't get until the 1980s. With the renaissance of mechanical watchmaking getting into swing, there was an increased interest in vintage diving watches, among the rarest, those made by Panerai and Rolex, with these dials combining two types of numerals. One of the stories about how the 'California dial' got its name is that vintage watch dealers played into the frenzy by having the dials of original Rolex Bubble Backs refinished. A man by the name of Kirk Rich was their go-to guy, and as he was based in California, the name kind of stuck with experts who used it to indicate these refinished dials. Among the general public, it quickly became the legitimate designation for all dials featuring this unique combination of numerals. At Isotope, the love for dive watches runs deep. With the Hydrium and HydriumX, a modern dive watch with a nod to vintage design was born. These timepieces embody the perfect fusion of architectural brilliance and horological excellence. Luis Revuelta, inspired by his journey in architecture, discovered the power of the yellow-and-black combination while studying. It not only provided a visually strong impact but also served as a personal identifier for his tools. The yellow and black reminded him of robust heavy equipment like International Harvesting, Caterpillar and the speed of vehicles like Porsche and Ferrari. During countless all-nighters, the yellow colour acted as a visual boost, evoking a sense of happiness during the late hours. It also helped organise his workspace, bringing order amidst clutter. The easy readability of yellow letters against a black background, or vice versa, further solidified his fondness for this colour combination. After being teased by family and friends for his yellow-only collection, he embraced blue as an alternative. He found blue clothes and blue dials to be elegant and unique, standing out from the typical black dials. The soothing nature of blue reminded him of the Caribbean waters, his birthplace of Cuba, and the Miami sky, his adopted home. Blue served as a counterbalance to the energetic yellow gadgets that surrounded him, providing a sense of tranquillity. For diving watches, the yellow dials on grey or black cases deliver a sharp, tough, and reliable appearance, coupled with exceptional legibility. The combination became the corporate colours that defined Luis's vision. His vision was also transported to the Hydrium Amarillo dial, a shimmering yellow, while the Hydrium Azul boasts a captivating matte blue. These limited editions of 50 + 50 watches by Luis Revuelta are now available for immediate delivery. Two of them will be symbolically delivered to the patrons HM King Charles III and HE President Marcelo Rebelo de Sousa, who participated in the recent London ceremony that reinforced the virtues of the Anglo-Portuguese alliance. Part of the proceeds will be given to ANDI — New Dialogue Organization, a charity active in Portugal and the UK. The Isotope Old Radium Portugal-UK 650 includes elements alluding to the maritime history of Portugal and the United Kingdom and debuts an unprecedented dial in the collection of the brand founded by José Mendes Miranda. The 40mm bronze case refers to the conquest of the seas — bronze being an alloy always used in a nautical environment. The white dial with a contrasting black outer ring for the minute scale features an enamel coating. The hands and numerals match the bronze on the case, while the textured leather strap with a bronze buckle provides an ideal complement. The titanium caseback is engraved with the number of the limited edition and the sapphire glass features elements of the coats of arms of Portugal and England in 1373 and 2023, revealing a 40-hour power reserve Swiss Landeron 24 automatic movement underneath. watches.description: Nasa approved - Limited edition Isotope Hydrium® NASA Isotope Hydrium NASA : A watch to love to the moon and back Space is one of the most hostile environments humankind has ever ventured into. Zero gravity, no oxygen, and extreme temperatures are just some of the challenges we face when exploring the universe. While complex to solve, an essential factor of what makes us the dominant species on Earth is that we collectively follow up on those dreams. In 1958 an important step to fulfilling them was made when the National Aeronautics and Space Act (Pub.L. 85-568) created the National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA) . It was NASA that first put humans on the surface of the moon. However, getting into space and exploring it is only part of the equation when it comes to manned spaceflight. Returning to our beautiful blue and green planet comes with its own set of challenges, as it means a volatile descent into the Earth's atmosphere. The reentry capsule starts to experience drag as it moves through the air, which can heat the surface of the capsule to up to a scorching 1,480 °C (2,700 °F). To ensure the safety of the astronauts, the reentry capsule is equipped with a heat shield. As it moves through the atmosphere toward the Earth, part of the heat shield cools the module by burning off. This not only plays a vital role in a safe return to Earth but also creates a unique distressed texture on the outside of the reentry module. For Isotope , this was the inspiration for the new Hydrium NASA . To replicate the texture, the 316L stainless steel case of the Hydrium NASA has a polymer-ceramic coating called Cerakote® . The applied coating creates a distressed look, making each case unique and exclusive. It sets the stage for the rest of the watch, with the dial as its main eyecatcher. While very clean in appearance, its different layers give it a sense of depth. The outer ring features a railroad track that makes it easy to read the minutes and seconds, which can be handy in case you have to manually time a controlled burn to ensure safe entry. Its dark blue colour matches not only the signature box-shaped hands of the Hydrium but also outline the Lacrima at the centre, Isotope 's logo. As NASA was just as over the moon with this watch as we are, they officially endorsed it. That's why its logo is at the six o'clock position, with its red colour matching that of the centrally mounted second hand. The dial is surrounded by a 120-clock bezel with minute/seconds markings with a unique feature; just like the dial, it is full lume. This makes for a spectacular sight, anywhere from the dark side of the moon and the dimmed lights of Cape Canaveral ground control to your living room watching 'Apollo 13' once again. The Super-LumiNova is also applied on the hands of the Hydrium NASA, further enhancing its visibility in low-light conditions. Born as a diving watch, it comes with a screw-down crown and 300m / 30 atm / 1000 ft water resistance, making it perfect for when the reentry module safely splashes into the ocean after a successful return flight. The Hydrium NASA features a double-domed sapphire crystal with an anti-reflective coating. Through its screw-down exhibition case back, the Swiss-made Landeron or La Joux-Perret movement is visible, offering a power reserve of 40 hours or 68 hours respectively . To ensure that the Hydrium NASA stays safely on your wrist during lift-off, space flight, reentry, and other earthly activities, Nick Mankey Designs created an exclusive strap for ISOTOPE featuring the NASA logo. It is one of those details that makes the Hydrium NASA even more out of this world. Please remember to add a note with your chosen NASA strap size at checkout. The Isotope Hydrium® NASA is limited to 200 pieces, so don't wait to see the far side of the moon to own one. watches.description: Limited Edition Hydrium® Pro Nordblad The Hydrium Pro Nordblad Limited Edition is a tribute to the remarkable achievements of Johanna Nordblad , a true champion and world-renowned ice diver. Her inspiring story of resilience and bravery has left an indelible mark on the Isotope team, and we are honoured to welcome her aboard for the second time. The new Isotope Hydrium® Pro is limited to 100 pieces and it's the first of a series of Hrydrium® PRO watches, exceeding specifications above ISO 6425, the official certification to be considered a Divers watch. The watch case is made of sandblasted 316L stainless steel. The crystals, including the bezel, are made of Sapphire Crystal and the movement is a top-finished and regulated Swiss Landeron. This specific version was designed in the United Kingdom and Finland , in collaboration with Johanna Nordblad and expertly assembled in Switzerland . Johanna 's journey began in 1997 when she first tried scuba diving. Although she enjoyed it, she quickly fell in love with freediving after joining the first freediving club in Finland in 2000. She went on to compete in the World Championships that same year. In 2004, Johanna broke a world record in Dynamic Apnea, and her passion for freediving only grew from there. However, in 2010, Johanna suffered a severe leg injury that required a fasciotomy and left her using crutches for almost a year. The nerve pain she experienced was so intense that she woke up almost every night for three years. It was during this difficult time that Johanna discovered the healing powers of cold water. At first, the cold was painful, but eventually, she found that it was the only place where she could find relief from her leg pain. She also discovered that the feeling of cold water was similar to the relaxation she experienced while freediving. As a result, Johanna became fascinated with the idea of combining cold water and freediving. She began practising in the most extreme conditions she could imagine, including under ice. In 2015, Johanna broke the Women’s World Record by diving under ice wearing only a swimming suit. She swam an impressive fifty meters from one hole in the ice to another. In March 2021, Johanna accomplished the incredible feat of becoming the first human to swim 103 meters under the ice without fins and while wearing only a swimsuit. Her time of apnea during the dive was an impressive 2 minutes and 42 seconds. While her record has since been beaten by men, Johanna still holds the Women's Record for this remarkable accomplishment. So impressive was her achievement that Netflix created a Bafta -nominated documentary about the preparations and the day Johanna became the world champion. Titled " Hold Your Breath: The Ice Dive ," the documentary takes viewers on a journey through Johanna's training, the physical and mental challenges she faced, and the exhilarating moment she made history. You can watch this incredible documentary on Netflix and be inspired by Johanna's remarkable achievement. Johanna 's dedication to the sport of freediving is unwavering, and her humility is an inspiration to us all. Despite her incredible achievements, she remains eager to learn more about herself and the sport that she loves. Her passion for freediving is contagious and has earned her respect and admiration from fellow athletes and fans alike. It is with great pride that we pay tribute to Johanna 's remarkable accomplishments with the Hydrium Pro Nordblad Limited Edition . This exclusive edition is a testament to her incredible journey and serves as a reminder of what can be achieved through hard work and determination. We are honoured to be associated with such an incredible athlete and look forward to witnessing her future successes in the sport of freediving. The Isotope Hydrium® Pro Nordblad is limited to 100 pieces, and it's now available. watches.name: Hydrium Alba
watches.description: Limited Edition of 100 numbered watches Isotope & Scottish Watches Team Up To Create The Hydrium Alba The identity of Scotland goes far beyond haggis, kilts, and bagpipes. As the most northern part of the United Kingdom, it offers some of the most breathtaking scenery and a welcome combination of nature, historic sites, and energetic cities. Scotland also plays an essential role in the history of Isotope. At a dinner party in Glasgow in 1913, radiochemist Frederick Soddy was discussing his discovery of radioelements with unique half-lives. As the Periodic Table has no room for them, a close friend of his wife, Dr Margaret Todd, suggested calling them Isotopes. A very appropriate name as in Greek, this means '(coming from the) same place.' Soddy adopted the name, publishing his theory in the December issue of 'Nature,' that same year and being awarded the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 1921. Like Isotope's straightforward approach to watchmaking, Scottish Watches also doesn't beat around the bush. Founded in 2019, their extraordinary expertise and honest point of view have resulted in a loyal following, even from far beyond the borders of Scotland. They are the second-largest watch-oriented podcast in the world, with over 400 episodes to date. Given Isotope's strong connection and love for Scotland in general, and the Island of Arran in particular, a unique partnership was born. The result is the Hydrium Alba. The name Alba comes from old Scottish Gaelic, referring to what we now know as Scotland. This no-nonsense diving watch comes with a new sense of refinement, representing the national colours of Scotland by combining a white enamel dial with beautiful heat-blued hands. The contrast between the rugged 40mm large case made of 316L stainless steel with a micro-blasted finish and the mysterious gloss provided by the enamel dial is a rarity in a diving watch. The Isotope Hydrium Alba is powered by a Swiss Landeron calibre 24. This automatic movement runs at 4Hz and offers a power reserve of 40 hours. To underscore the rugged nature of the watch, Isotope keeps this well-decorated movement hidden underneath a closed case back. However, a deep engraving of a divers' helmet ensures that the back of the Hydrium Alba remains as attractive to look at as the front. The precious enamel dial is protected by double-domed sapphire crystal, framed by a black 120-click bezel with a sapphire insert. Its understated appearance is strengthened by Isotope's decision to not include a date function, achieving a cleaner and more powerful appearance. With a water resistance of 300m/1.000 ft, the Hydrium Alba is perfect for underwater exploration of any of the over 30.000 freshwater 'lochs' you can find in Scotland. You want to wear this watch when launching your expedition to find the legendary monster of Loch Ness, although your time is probably better spent enjoying the beaches and hospitality of the island of Arran with it. Like the previous versions of the Hydrium, Isotope also printed a railroad track to mark the hours, minutes, and seconds on the dial of the Alba, this time opting for a blue colour matching the hue of the hands. As the brand's signature Lacrima and the index ring are slightly elevated, the enamel was increasingly difficult to apply. The challenges that this gave were, in the end, worth the trouble. The changes in height provide a wonderful play of light, in which the unique milky shimmer of the enamel comes even more to life, underscoring the fact that the Hydrium Alba isn't like any other diving watch. Like the original Moonshot Stealth , the Terra Maris features a world-first and exclusive sub-dial system that reimagines the tricompax layout for improved legibility. Beneath a striking double-domed sapphire crystal , the Moonshot’s futuristic design makes a bold statement in both form and function. Each piece is CNC-machined from a solid block of Grade 5 Titanium , DLC-coated, and hand-finished to achieve a sophisticated, matte aesthetic. Inside beats either a Swiss ETA Valjoux 7753 or Landeron 73 automatic movement. The distinctive 41mm case (49.5mm lug-to-lug) continues Isotope’s mission to reshape traditional chronograph design. Inspired by the sci-fi classic The Incal by Jodorowsky and Moebius , the Moonshot reflects founder José Miranda ’s deep love of graphic novels and space-age storytelling. (Note: The Incal and its authors are not affiliated with this project.) While the Stealth leans into deep space, the Terra Maris edition brings the design back to Earth with a colourway inspired by the land and sea, a gradient blend of browns and blues drawn from the Cascais coastline , where Seabra lives. It follows the original GMT 0º Terra Maris, extending the concept into a capsule collection . “The Terra Maris reflects my home by the Atlantic,” says Seabra. “It blends retro-futurism with the timeless beauty of coastal Portugal. I’m proud to collaborate with a microbrand as innovative as Isotope.” After four years of development, the Moonshot stands as Isotope’s most technically ambitious watch yet, featuring a bespoke and exclusive rotating sub-dial mechanism precisely calibrated for accuracy. Each Moonshot Terra Maris is individually numbered and delivered with a three-link Grade 5 Titanium bracelet and a blue cut-to-size FKM rubber strap , both with DLC butterfly deployant clasps. As with all Moonshots, production is limited by time and demand. About Miguel Seabra A graduate in History of Arts, Miguel Seabra has been travelling the world covering watches for 30 years and tennis for 34 years. He feels privileged to have both his passions for professions, even though he sometimes finds it hard to change the chip! Editor of Espiral do Tempo magazine and commentator for Eurosport, he is a member of the Academy and a former member of the jury of the Grand Prix d’Horlogerie de Genève and is also a member of the jury of the International Tennis Hall Of Fame. watches.description: GMT 0º Terra Maris Limited Edition in collaboration with Miguel Seabra Isotope proudly introduces the GMT 0º ‘Terra Maris’ Limited Edition , in collaboration with Miguel Seabra — one of the most experienced and iconic journalists of the watch (and tennis!) scene. The GMT 0º ‘Terra Maris’ is a limited run of 49 pieces and not only features a unique GMT + date display, but also a quite original colour combination inspired by the seaside. Here's Miguel Seabra ’s rationale behind the creation of the ‘ Terra Maris ’ concept: “When my friend José Mendes Miranda , founder of Isotope Watches , challenged me to come up with an idea for a limited edition of the GMT 0º , I pretty much envisioned a theme straight away since it had been on the back of my mind for a while. If I were to be associated with a timepiece, it would have to be quite different and boast an original colour combination. And... cool as well! So, being the GMT 0º a travel watch per definition, and being Isotope a watch brand based in a country ( England ) with the same time zone as mine ( Portugal ), I wanted it to reflect a bit the beautiful place where I live on the seaside and not only convey the idea of vacations but also casual elegance. To me, the epitome of casual elegance is a good pair of jeans coupled with brown suede shoes plus a white shirt and a nice blazer. Brown and blue also represent the land and the sea, and I live in the coastal resort of Cascais , at the most western point of Europe , where the continent ends and the ocean starts. Hence the Latin name, ‘ Terra Maris ’. The land and the sea, the brown and the blue, suede shoes and denim!”. “I am also proud to collaborate with a microbrand as offbeat as Isotope Watches . Microbrands have been doing a terrific job allowing easier access to the not so cheap world of mechanical watchmaking and/or providing a choice to those who prefer wearing something out of the box. The Isotope GMT 0º is an original timepiece, with its never before used combination of a GMT disc with a date displayed via a black dot shifting around the 31 holes on the dial”. “Another good point for a travel watch suited for summer destinations is the water resistance; the GMT 0º ‘Terra Maris’ is water-resistant to 200 meters due to its thick 3mm sapphire glass and screwed crown. It is robust enough to go dive with and wear on the beach. A reliable Swiss Landeron automatic movement makes it ready to go and wear anywhere, anytime”. “Of course, being a strapaholic myself, the GMT 0º ‘Terra Maris’ had to come with two choices: a metal bracelet with a clasp featuring three adjustment positions and a brown retro leather strap with blue stitching; but a black strap also works very well, matching the black tip of the ‘ Lacrima ’ on the centre of the dial, whereas a white or light blue strap would reinforce the holiday/summer aura of the watch”. “Two small details also make this limited edition special compared to other GMT 0º models: the ‘ Terra Maris ’ nomenclature discreetly engraved on the central GMT disc, whereas on the back the GMT zone indicated is Lisbon (not London ). A third asset is the luminescence on the hour markers beside the hour/minute hands and GMT dot, which doesn’t happen in the regular GMT 0º pieces of the collection”. “The GMT 0º ‘Terra Maris’ edition is limited to 49 individually numbered pieces. Why such an odd figure? Because ‘my number’ is Thirteen; only 13 watches would not be enough and 130 would be too many. But 4+9 equals 13; I hope it’ll be a lucky number for everyone who chooses to have one!”. watches.description: The Palloncino inspiration and concept For better or worse, our days are ruled by an inflexible reality - there are only 24 hours in a day, and oftentimes it feels that we have 36 hours of tasks to accomplish! At Isotope, we feel that time should be appreciated rather than blindly followed. Your day should be savoured rather than hurried through. You should be able to float through your day, rather than race madly through it. The Isotope Palloncino is our way of reminding ourselves that, although we need to be on time and function within our schedules, our days, our time, and our lives should be enjoyed, not worried over. The Palloncino di Perle (Mother of Pearl balloon) and the Palloncino d’Acciaio (Steel balloon). Savour time.
